flags: Pacira BioSciences entered into a merger agreement with Viatris Inc. under which Viatris will commence a cash tender offer to acquire all outstanding shares of Pacira common stock at $36.50 per share.

Pacira completed the divestiture of its iovera° business to Zimmer, Inc. (a subsidiary of Zimmer Biomet Holdings) for up to $140.0 million, receiving $73.6 million in cash after purchase price adjustments at closing.

Pacira recorded a full impairment of its $163.2 million goodwill balance during the year ended December 31, 2024, triggered by FDA approval of a generic competitor to EXPAREL and a court ruling invalidating an EXPAREL patent.

Royalty revenues are related to the sale of bupivacaine liposome injectable suspension for veterinary use.

business_model.basis: Stated in the 10-K MD&A revenue discussion.
business_model.claim: EXPAREL revenue growth is driven by gross vial volume, vial mix, and net selling price per unit, with GPO contracting and price increases as key price levers.
quotes: EXPAREL revenue increased 5% in 2025 versus 2024. Components of the increase included a 6% increase in gross vial volume, which was partially offset by a shift in vial mix and decreases in net selling price per unit in 2025 versus 2024. The decrease in net selling price per unit relates to increases in sales-related allowances as a result of group purchasing organization (GPO) contracting, partially offset by a January 2025 price increase.

business_model.basis: Stated in the 10-K MD&A revenue discussion.
business_model.claim: ZILRETTA revenue is driven by kit volume and net selling price per unit, with price increases partially offset by gross-to-net adjustments.
quotes: ZILRETTA revenue decreased 1% in 2025 versus 2024, primarily due to a 4% decrease in kit volume, partially offset by a 3% increase in net selling price per unit. The increase in net selling price per unit is related to two price increases in 2025, partially offset by higher gross-to-net adjustments.

business_model.basis: Stated in the 10-K Risk Factors and the Q2 2026 8-K earnings release.
business_model.claim: Third-party reimbursement policy, including the NOPAIN Act and payer-specific coverage decisions, is a critical driver of EXPAREL and ZILRETTA revenue.
quotes: Implementation of the NOPAIN Act in January 2025 now provides for separate reimbursement of qualifying non-opioids, like EXPAREL, administered during surgical procedures in the outpatient environment, is a significant policy advancement aimed at alleviating cost concerns for the Medicare population

UnitedHealthcare is now providing separate reimbursement for EXPAREL® (bupivacaine liposome injectable suspension) across outpatient settings, including hospital outpatient departments and ambulatory surgery centers.

business_model.basis: Stated in the 10-K MD&A overview and Risk Factors.
business_model.claim: EXPAREL is distributed via a drop-ship model directly to end-users with no product held by wholesalers, while ZILRETTA uses a buy-and-bill model where physicians hold inventory.
quotes: We drop-ship EXPAREL directly to end-users based on orders placed to wholesalers or directly to us, and there is no product held by wholesalers.
ZILRETTA is a physician-administered product, and therefore physicians are required to purchase and manage the inventory of ZILRETTA, prior to administering the product to patients.

business_model.basis: Stated in the 10-K MD&A cost of goods sold section.
business_model.claim: Cost of goods sold comprises labor, raw materials, manufacturing overhead, occupancy, depreciation, quality control, and engineering, and gross margin improved to 79% in 2025 from 76% in 2024.
quotes: Cost of goods sold primarily relates to the costs to produce, package and deliver our products to customers. These expenses include labor, raw materials, manufacturing overhead and occupancy costs, depreciation of facilities, quality control and engineering.

Gross margin increased three percentage points in 2025 versus 2024 primarily due to lower EXPAREL inventory reserves and improved ZILRETTA product costs due to higher volumes manufactured in order to enhance the level of inventory on hand, partially offset by accelerated depreciation of fixed assets impacted by the decommissioning of our 45-liter EXPAREL batch manufacturing suite at our Science Center Campus in San Diego, California

business_model.basis: Stated in the 10-K MD&A Science Center Campus Reduction in Force section.
business_model.claim: Pacira's manufacturing scale-up to 200+ liter batch suites (San Diego and Swindon, UK) produces approximately four-fold greater bulk EXPAREL volumes than the prior 45-liter process, improving unit cost and gross margin.
quotes: These two large-scale manufacturing suites are capable of producing bulk EXPAREL volumes that are approximately four-fold greater than our 45-liter batch manufacturing process, and we believe these larger manufacturing suites provide ample capacity for meeting the growing demand and improving gross margins for EXPAREL through a meaningfully more favorable cost structure and manufacturing yields versus the 45-liter batch process.

business_model.basis: Stated in the 10-K Business section Strategy subsection.
business_model.claim: Pacira's 5x30 strategy, launched January 2025, targets delivering products to more than three million patients annually, double-digit CAGR in product revenues, five-point gross margin improvement over 2024, at least five clinical pipeline programs, and five partnerships by 2030.
quotes: In January 2025, we launched our new 5x30 strategic growth plan ("5x30") to accelerate our transition into an innovative biopharmaceutical and therapeutic area leader in musculoskeletal pain and adjacencies. The 5x30 plan focuses on five key objectives that we intend to achieve by 2030: (i) deliver our products to more than three million patients annually; (ii) grow product revenues by a double-digit compounded annual growth rate; (iii) achieve a five percentage-point improvement in gross margins over 2024; (iv) advance an innovative pipeline with at least five programs in clinical development and (v) establish five partnerships—including pipeline and commercial agreements.

competitive_position.claim: In October 2025, two Chinese generic manufacturers (WhiteOak and Qilu) submitted ANDAs seeking FDA authorization for a generic version of EXPAREL, and Pacira filed a patent infringement suit against both in November 2025.

In November 2025, we filed a patent infringement suit against WhiteOak and Qilu.

competitive_position.claim: EXPAREL faces competition from opioids (morphine, fentanyl, meperidine, hydromorphone), NSAIDs (ketorolac, Caldolor), other local anesthetics (bupivacaine, marcaine, ropivacaine), elastomeric pumps, catheter devices, and at least one FDA-approved oral NaV1.8 inhibitor (suzetrigine).
quotes: Competing products available for postsurgical pain management include opioids such as morphine, fentanyl, meperidine and hydromorphone, each of which is available generically from several manufacturers
We are aware of at least one FDA-approved oral, non-opioid, highly selective NaV1.8 pain signal inhibitor that utilizes suzetrigine for the treatment of moderate-to-severe pain in adults.

competitive_position.claim: ZILRETTA competes with generic immediate-release steroids, HA-containing products, and stem cell and PRP injections for the management of OA knee pain.
quotes: ZILRETTA competes with immediate-release steroids and HA-containing products, as well as stem cell and PRP injections.

Immediate-release TA and other injectable immediate-release steroids, which are the current IA standard of care for OA pain, are available in generic form and are therefore relatively inexpensive compared to the pricing for ZILRETTA.

achieve a five percentage-point improvement in gross margins over 2024
We currently expect that tariffs will have a negative impact on gross margins.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in P6 (8-K) for the UnitedHealthcare update; stated in P2 (10-K Risk Factors) for NOPAIN Act and P&T committee risk; stated in P3 (10-K MD&A) for GPO contracting impact on net price.
growth_thesis.claim: Reimbursement expansion is a growth enabler: the NOPAIN Act (effective January 2025) provides separate Medicare reimbursement for qualifying non-opioids like EXPAREL in outpatient settings, and UnitedHealthcare (approximately 40 million covered lives) now provides separate reimbursement for EXPAREL outside the surgical bundle; for this driver to continue, additional large payers must adopt similar separate-reimbursement policies and GPO contracting must not erode net pricing.
quotes: UnitedHealthcare is now providing separate reimbursement for EXPAREL® (bupivacaine liposome injectable suspension) across outpatient settings, including hospital outpatient departments and ambulatory surgery centers.

Implementation of the NOPAIN Act in January 2025 now provides for separate reimbursement of qualifying non-opioids, like EXPAREL, administered during surgical procedures in the outpatient environment, is a significant policy advancement aimed at alleviating cost concerns for the Medicare population

The decrease in net selling price per unit relates to increases in sales-related allowances as a result of group purchasing organization (GPO) contracting, partially offset by a January 2025 price increase.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in P3 (10-K MD&A) for the LG Chem partnership terms and EU authorization; stated in P1 (10-K Business) for the 5x30 partnership objective and EU approval date.
growth_thesis.claim: International expansion through partnerships is a growth vector: in January 2026, Pacira entered a co-promotion agreement with LG Chem for exclusive EXPAREL commercialization in select Asia-Pacific markets (South Korea, Thailand) for a $2.0 million upfront payment plus tiered royalties, and EXPAREL already holds EU marketing authorization; for this to drive revenue, LG Chem must obtain marketing authorizations in 2026 and achieve commercial sales, and EU uptake must grow beyond the current limited contribution.
quotes: we entered into a partnership agreement with LG Chem designed to expand access to opioid-sparing postsurgical pain control for patients in select Asian-Pacific markets. Through this partnership, LG Chem has the exclusive rights to commercialize EXPAREL for postsurgical pain management in the region.
LG Chem plans to file for marketing authorizations in South Korea and Thailand in 2026.
In November 2020, the European Commission, or EC, granted marketing authorization for EXPAREL

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in P1 (10-K Business) for patient count, 5x30 target, and sNDA approval; stated in P3 (10-K MD&A) for sales force expansion and RIF details.
growth_thesis.claim: Patient volume growth under the 5x30 plan: Pacira reached 2.5 million patients in 2025 against a 2030 target of more than three million annually; for this trajectory to continue, the expanded sales force (grew in H2 2024), co-promotion agreements (J&J MedTech for ZILRETTA, LG Chem for EXPAREL Asia-Pacific), and new indication approvals (adductor canal block, sciatic nerve block) must translate into incremental procedure utilization.
quotes: In 2025, we reached 2.5 million patients; volume trends show we are moving towards our goal of double-digit topline growth
deliver our products to more than three million patients annually

In November 2023, the FDA approved our supplementary New Drug Application, or sNDA, to expand the EXPAREL label to include administration in adults as an adductor canal block and a sciatic nerve block in the popliteal fossa.

material_events.claim: Pacira BioSciences entered into a merger agreement with Viatris Inc. under which Viatris will commence a cash tender offer to acquire all outstanding shares of Pacira common stock at $36.50 per share.
quotes: at an offer price of $36.50 per Share in cash, net of applicable withholding taxes and without interest (the "Offer Price").

material_events.basis: Stated in the Q2 2026 10-Q (filed August 6, 2026) and the Q2 2026 earnings 8-K (filed August 6, 2026).
material_events.claim: Pacira completed the divestiture of its iovera° business to Zimmer, Inc. (a subsidiary of Zimmer Biomet Holdings) for up to $140.0 million, receiving $73.6 million in cash after purchase price adjustments at closing.
quotes: The transaction closed on July 31, 2026 and the Company received cash of $73.6 million, after purchase price adjustments.

material_events.claim: Pacira recorded a full impairment of its $163.2 million goodwill balance during the year ended December 31, 2024, triggered by FDA approval of a generic competitor to EXPAREL and a court ruling invalidating an EXPAREL patent.
quotes: the then-goodwill balance of $163.2 million was recorded as fully impaired during the year ended December 31, 2024.

material_events.claim: Pacira instituted a reduction in force at its Science Center Campus in San Diego impacting 71 employees (approximately 8% of workforce) and decommissioned its 45-liter EXPAREL batch manufacturing suite, recognizing $3.7 million in termination charges, $1.0 million in inventory reserves, and $5.5 million in accelerated depreciation.
quotes: In July 2025, as a result of improving manufacturing efficiencies for EXPAREL, we instituted a reduction in force at our Science Center Campus in San Diego, California.

material_events.claim: Pacira filed a patent infringement suit against WhiteOak and Qilu, two Chinese generic manufacturers that had submitted ANDAs seeking FDA authorization to market a generic version of EXPAREL in the U.S.
quotes: In November 2025, we filed a patent infringement suit against WhiteOak and Qilu.

risks.claim: EXPAREL, which generated 79% of 2025 total revenues, faces generic entry after two Paragraph IV certifications from WhiteOak and Qilu in October 2025 and a prior FDA-approved generic competitor in 2024 that also triggered a $163.2 million goodwill impairment.
quotes: During 2025, sales of EXPAREL accounted for 79% of our total revenue, and we expect EXPAREL sales will remain of primary importance for the foreseeable future.

In October 2025, we received two separate Paragraph IV Certifications from two Chinese generic drug manufacturers—WhiteOak and Qilu—each advising that they had submitted an ANDA to the FDA seeking authorization from the FDA to manufacture, use or sell a generic version of EXPAREL in the U.S.
During the year ended December 31, 2024, the FDA approved a generic competitor to EXPAREL and a U.S. District Court ruled that one of our EXPAREL patents was not valid.

risks.basis: Stated in P2 (Risk Factors) and P3 (MD&A revenue table). The 79% and 16% figures are from the 10-K revenue discussion. The concentration risk language is explicit.
